title: Read container logs
summary: Logs record messages written by a container's program. They help explain what it is doing or why it stopped.
introduction: Logs record messages written by a container's program. They help explain what it is doing or why it stopped. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Logs record messages written by a container's program. They help explain what it is doing or why it stopped.
The command prints available logs for the named practice container. Reading logs does not restart it.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Visit the practice page and look for a new request entry.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not put secrets into logs; logs are often copied elsewhere.
For more detail later, use this [Docker further reading](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/).

seo.title: Docker: Read container logs
seo.description: Learn about read container logs in Docker. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
